newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus c.bank buys 100 bln rbs of Russia T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Belarus c.bank buys 100 bln rbs of Russia T-bills.

text.p: Russia's central Bank, keen to promote the rouble as a reserve currency for former Soviet republics, has allowed the central bank of Belarus to buy Russian Treasury bills, a senior Russian bank official said.

The National Bank of Belarus has bought about 100 billion roubles of GKO discount Treasury bills, switching some of its reserves into Russian roubles, central bank First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told a news conference on Monday.
"We think the terms offered by the Central Bank of Russia for placing hard currency reserves of neighbouring countries in roubles are more attractive than holding them in dollars," he said.
Aleksashenko said the National Bank of Belarus had the right to carry out all operations on the T-bill market and has the same rights as a Russian resident.
He said the size of Belarus's investment had no impact on the market.
"Such a volume cannot influence the market," Aleksashenko said. "We can increase investment in the market easily both from the National Bank of Belarus and other national banks."
On Monday the trade turnover on government securities market was a low 1.80 trillion roubles.
Aleksashenko said the Russian central bank was in talks on similar agreements with the central banks of Ukraine and Kazakhstan, but these banks had not yet taken a decision.
